Fibroblast foci. Discrete bulges of immature fibroblasts in amphophilic matrix are referred to as fibroblast or fibroblastic foci. They occur at the interface between dense scar and adjacent normal lung. In a three-dimensional reconstruction study, the foci appear to be interconnected into a lattice. These lesions are thought to be the focus of ongoing injury and repair in usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP), but are not unique to UIP. H&E stain, 200xoriginal magnification.

full.description: This is a photomicrograph of a blood vessel, likely from a tissue biopsy showing signs of necrotizing vasculitis. The image displays marked inflammation of the vessel wall with fibrinoid necrosis and infiltration of inflammatory cells. A dense cellular infiltrate surrounds the compromised vessel structure, including lymphocytes and neutrophils. These histopathological findings are characteristic of a systemic vasculitis or an immune-mediated vascular injury.

blind.description: This is a micrograph of lung tissue stained with H&E. The image displays characteristic fibroblast foci, which appear as discrete bulges of immature fibroblasts within an amphophilic matrix at the interface between dense scar and normal lung. These findings are indicative of ongoing lung injury and repair, commonly seen in usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP).

random.description: This is a microscopic histopathology image showing a blood vessel with fibrinoid necrosis of the wall and surrounding inflammatory infiltrates. The vessel wall exhibits bright pink, amorphous material indicative of fibrinoid necrosis and transmural inflammation. These findings are characteristic of vasculitis, such as polyarteritis nodosa or ANCA-associated vasculitis. The tissue section is stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E).
